title: Wilber's own reed, mouthpiece and fingering background
summary: Wilber uses a number five Van Doren with a close lay; Bechet gave no fingering advice because Wilber had classical study with Arey and others.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: What kind of a read did you learn to use or like best?
Well, I ended up using a Van Doren. About what number? Well, I used a number five.
But I used a close symphonic lead.

You think you can get as big a tone that way as with a wider? Bigger, I feel it. You can get bigger. I thought maybe it was the other way around. Well, it's... You couldn't blow so much air through it or something.
There's more resistance, but you can really push the air through and get a big... You can get a hard read.
It all depends. A hard read on a close mouthpiece won't be like a hard read on a more open mouthpiece. You know, it's all... You get the right relationship between the mouthpiece and the read.

Well, I think I did... It was just about out of tape here. If you feel like going another half hour, I think we can find a few more questions to ask. Okay. I was going to ask, did Sidney ever demonstrate or advise anything like the different forked fingerings? Down here in place, they're calling it... What's the usual word for it? Is it... I can't think.

Yeah. Some others. Is it cross finger? No, no. I can't think of the name. But they call it forked fingerings down here. Yeah, yeah. You know, when they leave one finger... Did he ever discuss anything of those kind of...

No, he didn't because of the fact that he played Albert and I played Bane. Oh, that's right. And I had a fairly good basic knowledge of the fingering of the instrument from legitimate study by then, you know. I studied under Rufus Airy up at Eastman. Oh, that's right. Legitimate. And I studied with a man named Dom who played with the Goldman Band in New York. And I'd gone through the Bane, the Lazarus books and the Closet and all those studies.
